entities.evidence: Noah invokes אֱלֹהִים, God, as the one who can make room for Japheth. The verb יַפְתְּ has singular agreement.
Noah asks God to make room for his son Japheth, Shem’s brother.
The tents belong to Shem, Noah’s son and Japheth’s brother.
Noah names Canaan, Ham’s son, as the one who is to be a slave, continuing his pronouncement in Genesis 9:25–26.

analysis.evidence: In יַפְתְּ אֱלֹהִים לְיֶפֶת, God is the subject and לְיֶפֶת identifies the beneficiary: “May God give space to Japheth.” The verb יַפְתְּ echoes Japheth’s name, and the following וְיִשְׁכֹּן continues the blessing with another wish.
analysis.morphology: Hiphil jussive, third person masculine singular. The final ה of the root drops in this shortened form. There is no attached particle or pronominal suffix.
Masculine plural absolute common noun with singular verbal agreement.

analysis.evidence: In יַפְתְּ אֱלֹהִים לְיֶפֶת, Noah asks God to make room for Japheth. The verb יַפְתְּ echoes the sound of the name יֶפֶת.
analysis.morphology: The prefixed preposition לְ marks Japheth as the beneficiary. יֶפֶת is a personal name.

analysis.evidence: בְּאָהֳלֵי שֵׁם gives the place of dwelling, “in the tents of Shem.” The surrounding wishes for Japheth and Canaan favor taking Japheth as the one who will dwell there, though אֱלֹהִים is also a possible subject.
analysis.morphology: וְ is the conjunction “and.” יִשְׁכֹּן is Qal, third-person masculine singular. Its form also fits the imperfect, but the blessing gives it jussive force.
analysis.sense: dwell or live in a place

analysis.evidence: וְיִשְׁכֹּן בְּאָהֳלֵי שֵׁם means “and may he dwell in the tents of Shem.” The verb “dwell” supports the reading “tents” as places of habitation.
analysis.morphology: The preposition בְּ means “in.” אָהֳלֵי is the masculine plural construct of אֹהֶל, with שֵׁם (Shem) as its possessor.

analysis.evidence: In בְּאָהֳלֵי שֵׁם, “in the tents of Shem,” the personal name identifies whose tents are meant. The verse also names Japheth and Canaan. The source gloss “Paran” has no support in the text.
analysis.morphology: Hebrew personal name with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: The jussive continues Noah’s wish. כְנַעַן is the subject, and עֶבֶד names the status wished for him: “and may Canaan be a servant to them.”
analysis.morphology: The conjunction וִ precedes the short Qal jussive, third person masculine singular, agreeing with כְנַעַן.
analysis.sense: to be in a state or condition

analysis.morphology: Hebrew proper noun with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וִיהִי כְנַעַן עֶבֶד לָמוֹ, “may Canaan be a slave to them,” עֶבֶד names the status wished upon Canaan. The separate phrase לָמוֹ identifies whom he would serve.
analysis.morphology: Masculine singular common noun in the absolute state, with no prefix or suffix.

analysis.evidence: In וִיהִי כְנַעַן עֶבֶד לָמוֹ, “may Canaan be a servant to them,” עֶבֶד gives Canaan’s role and לָמוֹ identifies whom he is to serve. Japheth and Shem, both named earlier in the verse, supply a natural plural referent.
analysis.morphology: The preposition לְ appears as לָ־ before the poetic third-person masculine plural pronominal suffix מוֹ.
analysis.sense: Marks those whom Canaan is to serve.
